record.title: The star-with-loops homomorphism-density conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular simple graph. Let $S_k^o$ denote the graph obtained from the star $S_k$ by adding a loop at each vertex, and let $p_H(G)$ denote the normalized homomorphism density from $G$ to $H$.

**Star-with-loops conjecture.** For $d\geq 4$,

$$
p_{S_4^o}(G)\leq p_{S_4^o}(K_{d+1}).
$$

Furthermore, for $k\geq 6$,

$$
p_{S_k^o}(G)\leq p_{S_k^o}(K_{d,d}).
$$

These assertions propose complete or complete bipartite extremizers for homomorphism densities associated with stars having loops, extending the paper's discussion of extremal targets for regular graphs.
record.source_name: Emma Cohen, Péter Csikvári, Will Perkins and Prasad Tetali, “The Widom-Rowlinson model, the hard-core model and the extremality of the complete graph”, arXiv:1606.03718 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03718

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

record.title: Karzanov–Lomonosov conjecture on the size of cross-free families
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $2^{[n]}$ be the family of all subsets of $[n]$, and call two sets crossing when $A\setminus B$, $B\setminus A$, $A\cap B$, and $[n]\setminus(A\cup B)$ are all non-empty. A family $\mathcal{F}\subset 2^{[n]}$ is **$k$-cross-free** if it does not contain $k$ pairwise crossing sets.

**Karzanov–Lomonosov conjecture.** Let $k\geq 2$ and let $n$ be positive integers. If $\mathcal{F}\subset 2^{[n]}$ is a $k$-cross-free family, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|=O_k(n).
$$

This conjecture is known for $k=2$ and $k=3$, while for $k>3$ it remains open. The best general bound established in the paper is $O_k(n\log^* n)$, improving the earlier $O_k(n\log n)$ bound.
record.source_name: Andrey Kupavskii, János Pach and István Tomon, “On the size of k-cross-free families”, arXiv:1704.02175 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.02175

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2017). “For $k>3$, Conjecture remains open.”

record.title: Exact-recovery phase-transition conjecture for logarithmic-degree Euclidean random graphs
record.statement:
For any $\lambda>0$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$, and $0\leq b<a\leq 1$, let $\nu_d$ denote the volume of the unit Euclidean ball in $d$ dimensions, and let $G_n\sim\mathcal{G}_n(\lambda n,a,b,d)$ be the graph model whose connection functions are $f_{in}^{(n)}(r)=a\mathbf{1}_{r\leq\log(n)^{1/d}}$ and $f_{out}^{(n)}(r)=b\mathbf{1}_{r\leq\log(n)^{1/d}}$. **Exact-recovery phase-transition conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda\nu_d\left(1-\sqrt{ab}-\sqrt{(1-a)(1-b)}\right)>1,
$$

then Exact-Recovery of $G_n$ is solvable. The preceding theorem establishes impossibility when the same expression is less than $1$, so this conjecture identifies the threshold for Exact-Recovery in this simplest logarithmic-degree instance of the model; the authors state that they do not pursue a proof.
record.source_name: Emmanuel Abbe, Francois Baccelli and Abishek Sankararaman, “Community Detection on Euclidean Random Graphs”, arXiv:1706.09942 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.09942

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

record.title: The Leader–Spink maze solvability conjecture with one-column vertical gaps
record.statement: Let HNEs and VNEs denote horizontal and vertical edges removed from the square lattice maze, respectively. Consider mazes with arbitrarily many HNEs and arbitrarily many VNEs in one column. **One-column maze solvability conjecture.** There exists an algorithm that solves the set of all such mazes. This is posed in the paper's open-problems section as a problem expected to require techniques similar to those developed in the paper; its status is open.
record.source_name: Stefan David and Marius Tiba, “Solvability of Mazes by Blind Robots”, arXiv:1804.05439 (2018).

record.title: Strong bunk bed connectivity criterion
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $X$ be a specified collection of vertices with outside edges, and let $s$ and $f$ be the vertices considered in the bunk bed conjecture. Let $G-X$ denote the subgraph induced by removing the vertices in $X$. **Strong bunk bed criterion.** The graph satisfies the bunk bed conjecture strongly if and only if there is a path from $s$ to $f$ in $G-X$.

This is a proposed characterization of when the comparison in the bunk bed conjecture is strict. The source gives a proof framework involving path shadows and conditional connection probabilities, but does not state that the criterion is independently established beyond that discussion.
record.source_name: Andrew Lohr, “Several Topics in Experimental Mathematics”, arXiv:1805.00076 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.00076

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

record.title: Normalized-Laplacian form of the Ferrers bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph on $n\geq 3$ vertices with parts $X$ and $Y$, and let $\rho(G)=|E(G)|/(|X||Y|)$ be its bipartite density. If $G$ is connected, let $\mu_1\geq\cdots\geq\mu_{n-1}>\mu_n=0$ denote the eigenvalues of its normalized Laplacian. **Normalized-Laplacian Ferrers bound conjecture.** One has

$$
\prod_{i=1}^{n-2}\mu_i\leq \rho(G).
$$

The source states that this is equivalent to the Ferrers bound conjecture, so it is a restatement rather than a separate assertion. The supplied status is unknown, and the claim should therefore be treated as open unless its equivalence is resolved elsewhere.
record.source_name: Ravindra Bapat, “Maximizing spectral radius and number of spanning trees in bipartite graphs”, arXiv:1809.10342 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.10342

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2018).

record.title: The cycle independence-equivalence conjecture
record.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on $n$ vertices, let $D_n$ be the graph obtained from $C_n$ by adding a loop structure as defined in the paper, and let $[C_n]$ denote the independence equivalence class of $C_n$, namely the graphs having the same independence polynomial as $C_n$. **Cycle independence-equivalence conjecture.** If $3\!\!\!\not\vert n$ and $n\ge 4$, then

$$
[C_n]=\{C_n,D_n\}.
$$

This conjecture gives the expected complete description of the independence equivalence classes of cycles whose lengths are not divisible by $3$. The paper notes that multiples of $3$ can have triangle components and that the behavior of such cycles is more complicated; the proposed statement concerns the remaining cycle lengths.
record.source_name: Iain Beaton, Jason I. Brown and Ben Cameron, “Independence Equivalence Classes of Paths and Cycles”, arXiv:1810.05317 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.05317

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2018).

record.title: The c=1 and c=-2 tau-function correspondence conjecture
record.statement: Let $u=q^{2\sigma}$ and let $\tau$ and $\uptau$ denote the $c=1$ and $c=-2$ Painlevé VI tau functions, respectively. Let $\td{u}=\td{u}(u)$ and $\td{s}=\td{s}(s,\sigma)$ be functions, and let $f(u;q)$ and $h_k(u;q)$, $k=0,t,1,\infty$, be functions that are $q$-periodic in $z$. **Tau-function correspondence conjecture.** There exist such functions satisfying the four displayed identities relating the $c=1$ and $c=-2$ tau functions. The conjecture is motivated by the expected general-solution interpretation of the preceding $q$-Painlevé VI tau-function conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: M. Bershtein and A. Shchechkin, “Painleve equations from Nakajima-Yoshioka blowup relations”, arXiv:1811.04050 (2019).
record.references:

record.title: Conjecture on log-concavity of the signed binomial-Eulerian polynomials
record.statement:
For $n\geq1$, let $\tilde{A}_n(t,q)$ denote the $q$-binomial-Eulerian polynomial, and specialize it at $q=-1$ to obtain the signed binomial-Eulerian polynomial $\tilde{A}_n(t,-1)$. A polynomial $h(t)=\sum_{k=0}^na_k t^k$ is **log-concave** when its coefficients satisfy $a_k^2-a_{k-1}a_{k+1}\geq0$ for the relevant indices $k$.

**The signed log-concavity conjecture.** The polynomial $\tilde{A}_n(t,-1)$ is log-concave for $n\geq1$.

This is the second conjecture proposed in the closing remarks. The supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Zhicong Lin, David G. L. Wang and Jiang Zeng, “Around the q-binomial-Eulerian polynomials”, arXiv:1812.09098 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.09098

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).

record.title: Reiher–Schacht conjecture on constant rooted clique densities
record.statement:
Let $r\ge 3$ and let $W$ be a graphon. For $x,y\in[0,1]$, write $t_{x,y}(K_r^{\bullet\bullet},W)$ for the rooted homomorphism density of the clique $K_r$ with two distinguished roots, and let $V_W^{(r)}(x,y)=t_{x,y}(K_r^{\bullet\bullet},W)$. Suppose that

$$
V_W^{(r)}\equiv d
$$

for some $d\in[0,1]$. **Reiher–Schacht conjecture.** Then $W$ is $K_r$-free when $d=0$, or

$$
W\equiv d^{1/{\binom r 2}}.
$$

This characterizes graphons whose rooted $K_r$-density graphon is constant: apart from the $K_r$-free case, the graphon should be constant. The conjecture is posed for $r\ge 3$ and is attributed in the source to concluding remarks of Reiher and Schacht; no resolution is given here.

record.title: The undecidability conjecture for infinite stature in graphs of free groups
record.statement: Let $G$ be a group that splits as a finite graph of finitely generated free groups. An algorithm is said to certify that $G$ has infinite stature with respect to its vertex groups if, on input $G$, it outputs such a certification. **Undecidability conjecture.** There is no algorithm that takes as input $G$ and outputs a certification that $G$ has infinite stature with respect to its vertex groups. This is posed as an expected consequence after a proposition characterizing finite stature for graphs of groups with finite-index edge groups; the source provides no resolution or supporting evidence beyond this expectation.
record.source_name: Jingyin Huang and Daniel T. Wise, “Stature and separability in graphs of groups”, arXiv:1904.06021 (2019).

record.title: The critical-window product conjecture for random digraph components
record.statement:
Let $D(n,p)$ be the random directed graph and $G(n,p)$ the random graph, with $p=n^{-1}+\lambda n^{-4/3}$. Let $X^\lambda=n^{-2/3}|\mathcal{C}_1(G(n,p))|$ and $Y^\lambda=n^{-1/3}|\mathcal{C}_1(D(n,p))|$, and let $X_1^\lambda$ and $X_2^\lambda$ be independent copies of $X^\lambda$. **Critical-window product conjecture.** The distributions satisfy

$$
Y^\lambda=X_1^\lambda X_2^\lambda.
$$

This conjecture proposes an exact relation between the critical-window component-size distributions of random directed and undirected graphs, extending the known connection between giant strongly connected components in $D(n,p)$ and giant components in $G(n,p)$ for larger $p$.
record.source_name: Matthew Coulson, “The critical window in random digraphs”, arXiv:1905.00624 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.00624

record.title: The $p$-centered coloring conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement: A **$p$-centered coloring** of a graph is a vertex coloring such that every connected subgraph either receives more than $p$ colors or has a color appearing exactly once. **Planar graph coloring conjecture.** Planar graphs admit $p$-centered colorings with $\mathcal{O}(p^2\log p)$ colors. This is posed as one of the paper's further directions; the supplied source does not indicate whether the bound has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Michał Dębski, Stefan Felsner, Piotr Micek and Felix Schröder, “Improved bounds for centered colorings”, arXiv:1907.04586 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.04586

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: Admissible-subgraph density conjecture for partial subdivisions of complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $t\geq 3$, let $\mathcal{H}$ be the family of partial subdivisions of $K_t$, and let $(Q,\phi)$ be the weighted graph object used in the admissibility framework. An **$H$-admissible subgraph** is the admissible configuration defined in that framework for $H\in\mathcal{H}$, and $\phi(Q)$ denotes the corresponding total weight.

**Admissible-subgraph density conjecture.** If $(Q,\phi)$ has no $H$-admissible subgraph for any $H\in\mathcal{H}$, then

$$
\phi(Q)\geq \frac{1}{t-1}.
$$

The source says that proving this statement would suffice to prove the generalized weak-subdivision conjecture, because this is the only part of the preceding proof that does not apply to general families of graphs $\mathcal{H}$. The supplied context does not provide a resolution of this auxiliary conjecture.
record.source_name: Istvan Tomon, “A sharp threshold phenomenon in string graphs”, arXiv:1908.05550 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.05550

record.title: Classification conjecture for maximally generically transitive actions
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected group of finite Morley rank acting faithfully, definably and transitively on a set $X$ of Morley rank $n$, and suppose the action is generically $(n+2)$-transitive. **Maximal generic-transitivity conjecture.** The permutation group $(G,X)$ is definably equivalent to $(\operatorname{PGL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{K}),\mathbb{P}^n(\mathbb{K}))$ for some definable field $\mathbb{K}$. This conjecture explains the expected sharp bound on generic transitivity. It is known for $n=1$ and $n=2$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Alexandre Borovik and Adrien Deloro, “Binding groups, permutations groups and modules of finite Morley rank”, arXiv:1909.02813 (2019).

record.title: Log-concavity conjecture for Clar covering polynomials
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a hexagonal system, and let its Clar covering polynomial be

$$
\chi(H,x)=\sum_{k=0}^{C(H)}c(H,k)x^k,
$$

where $c(H,k)$ is the number of Clar covers of $H$ having precisely $k$ hexagons. **Log-concavity conjecture for Clar covering polynomials.** The Clar covering polynomial of a hexagonal system has log-concave coefficients. Numerical results motivate this conjecture, which is presented as open in the source.
record.source_name: Guanru Li, Lily Li Liu and Yi Wang, “Analytic properties of sextet polynomials of hexagonal systems”, arXiv:1912.03680 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.03680

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2019).

record.title: Shalaby's strong Skolem starter conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n$ be an integer with $n\geq11$, and let $\mathbb{Z}_n$ be the additive cyclic group of order $n$. A **strong Skolem starter** is a starter for $\mathbb{Z}_n$ that is both Skolem and strong. **Shalaby's conjecture.** If

$$
n\equiv1,3\pmod{8},
$$

then $\mathbb{Z}_n$ admits a strong Skolem starter. The conjecture gives the expected existence criterion for strong Skolem starters beyond the orders for which explicit constructions were known. The supplied text does not establish the conjecture in full; the later result in the paper concerns only specified families of orders.
record.source_name: Adrián Vázquez-Ávila, “On strong Skolem starters for Z_pq”, arXiv:2001.02220 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1907.05266](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.05266).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02220

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2020).

record.title: Azar et al.'s stationary-probability boosting conjecture for biased random walks
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $p$ be the stationary probability of a vertex under simple random walk, and let $
obreak\varepsilon$ be the controller's bias parameter. **Azar et al.'s conjecture.** In any graph, a controller can increase the stationary probability of any vertex from $p$ to $p^{1-\varepsilon}$.

The conjecture is false for $K_2$, and the paper explains that additional technical conditions are needed in the original formulation. It motivates the refined conjecture that allows an error term in the exponent.
record.source_name: John Haslegrave, Thomas Sauerwald and John Sylvester, “Time Dependent Biased Random Walks”, arXiv:2006.02475 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.02475

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Liu and Postle's density conjecture for triangle-free 4-critical graphs
record.statement:
A graph $G$ is **4-critical** if it is $4$-colourable but every proper subgraph is $3$-colourable; it is **triangle-free** if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $K_3$. Write $v(G)=|V(G)|$ and $e(G)=|E(G)|$. **Liu and Postle's density conjecture.** If $G$ is a $4$-critical triangle-free graph, then

$$
e(G) \geq \frac{5v(G)+5}{3}.
$$

This conjecture seeks a sharper lower-order improvement to the general Kostochka–Yancey edge bound for critical graphs after excluding triangles. The source gives no resolution status for the conjecture.
record.source_name: Benjamin Moore and Evelyne Smith-Roberge, “A density bound for triangle-free 4-critical graphs”, arXiv:2012.01503 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.01503

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Chern–Fu–Tang conjecture on log-concavity of k-colored partitions
record.statement:
Let $p_{-k}(n)$ denote the number of $k$-colored partitions of $n$, with $p_{-k}(n)=P_n(k)$, where $P_0(x)=1$ and

$$
P_n(x):=\frac{x}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n\sigma(j)P_{n-j}(x),\qquad \sigma(j):=\sum_{d\mid j}d.
$$

**Chern–Fu–Tang conjecture.** Let $n>m\geq 1$ and $k\geq 2$. Except for $(k,n,m)=(2,6,4)$,

$$
p_{-k}(n-1)p_{-k}(m+1)\geq p_{-k}(n)p_{-k}(m).
$$

This is a Bessenrodt–Ono-type log-concavity inequality for colored partition numbers. The source does not provide a resolution status for the conjecture.
record.source_name: Bernhard Heim and Markus Neuhauseer, “Proof of the Bessenrodt–Ono inequality by Induction”, arXiv:2108.00191 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2011.11056](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11056).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.00191

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).
